question: A train travels the first 100 km at 50 km/h and the next 100 km at 25 km/h. What is the average speed for the total journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When equal distances are covered at two different speeds x and y, the average speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y)

Here, x = 50 km/h and y = 25 km/h

Average Speed = (2 × 50 × 25) ÷ (50 + 25)

⇒ Average Speed = 2500 ÷ 75 = 100 ÷ 3 = 33.33 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance 1 (D₁) = 100 km, Speed 1 (S₁) = 50 km/h

Distance 2 (D₂) = 100 km, Speed 2 (S₂) = 25 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 100 km @ 50 km/h
 100 km @ 25 km/h
 
 
 Time = 2 hours
 Time = 4 hours
 
 
 Total: 200 km in 6 hours

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken for the first 100 km (T₁) = 100 ÷ 50 = 2 hours

⇒ Time taken for the next 100 km (T₂) = 100 ÷ 25 = 4 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 100 + 100 = 200 km

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 4 = 6 hours

⇒ Average Speed = 200 ÷ 6 = 100 ÷ 3

⇒ Average Speed = 33.33 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Unequal Distances

When distances covered are unequal, you must use the basic formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. You cannot simply average the speeds.

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If a journey is divided into three equal parts covered at speeds x, y, and z, the average speed is (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). When they move in the same direction, it is their difference (S₁ − S₂).
